event_name: Amyl and the Sniffers at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb:
Amyl and the Sniffers are the kind of band that critics and music nerds have been talking about for a few years now, and their live show is the reason why. The Australian punk outfit is loud, chaotic, and reportedly one of the most physically intense performances you'll see in a mid-size venue. Amy Taylor doesn't do reserved.

They're at the Coca-Cola Roxy on Sunday, October 4th. If you've been curious about them and haven't pulled the trigger on a show yet, this is a good opportunity — they don't come through Atlanta constantly. Sunday night is what it is, but for the right crowd, that's not a dealbreaker.

Check the Roxy's site for tickets and know-before-you-go info before heading out.
scoring_notes: Amyl and the Sniffers are a legitimately unique live act and their audience tends to skew younger and more musically adventurous. The Perimeter mix includes enough young professionals to make this relevant, but Sunday night timing and niche genre somewhat limit the reach. Worth including for the segment of the audience who follows indie/punk closely.

blurb:
Kany Garcia is one of the biggest names in Latin pop right now, a Grammy winner with a following that is deeply, genuinely devoted. If you know her work, you already understand why this show is worth a Thursday night. If you don't, here's the quick version: powerful vocals, emotionally honest songwriting, and a live show that tends to feel like a real event rather than just a concert.

She's at the Coca-Cola Roxy on October 1st. The Roxy is a great room for this kind of show — close enough that the performance actually lands, big enough that there's real energy in the crowd. Thursday nights aren't always easy to commit to, but this one has a legitimate case.

Tickets won't stick around forever on this one.
scoring_notes: Kany Garcia is a strong artist with a passionate fanbase, but the Perimeter audience demo doesn't skew heavily toward Latin pop. Still a good event worth surfacing for the portion of the audience that knows her. Thursday night timing is a slight friction point. Lower audience match score reflects niche genre fit rather than any quality issue with the event itself.

blurb:
Bleachers is one of those bands that a certain slice of the population is absolutely obsessed with, and everyone else hasn't quite discovered yet. If you're in the first group, you already know you need to be at the Roxy on October 5th. If you're in the second group, this is a good time to fix that.

Jack Antonoff's project has been building toward something for a while now, and their live show has a reputation for being genuinely electric — big, anthemic, emotionally sincere in a way that a lot of indie pop never quite pulls off. The Coca-Cola Roxy is one of the best mid-size venues in Atlanta, which makes a Monday night show there feel like less of a sacrifice than it probably should.

Monday shows at the Roxy don't fill themselves. Grab tickets before this one sneaks past you.
scoring_notes: Bleachers skews toward the 30-something, educated, indie-leaning crowd that makes up a solid chunk of the Perimeter audience. The Battery/Roxy is a familiar venue for this demographic. Monday night is a slight friction point, but the audience's income and lifestyle make a weeknight show feasible. Solid but not a slam dunk.

blurb:
Smoked meat, live bluegrass, and a bourbon tasting experience all in one place on a Saturday afternoon. That's the pitch, and honestly it doesn't need much more than that.

The Bourbon, BBQ & Bluegrass Festival rolls into Roswell on September 26th at You42 Studios, running 2–8 PM. The lineup covers live bluegrass, southern rock, and country all day. Local BBQ vendors and food trucks are on-site, local makers and craft vendors fill out the floor, and there's a full bar plus a dedicated bourbon tasting experience for the 21+ crowd. There's also a kids' area, so if you're bringing the family, you're covered.

This is the kind of Saturday that doesn't require a plan — just show up hungry, find a spot near the stage, and let it unfold. September evenings in Georgia are finally starting to feel like fall, and this is a solid way to spend one.
scoring_notes: Roswell is a bit outside the Perimeter core, but the event's adult-leaning profile (bourbon tasting, live music) fits the audience well. Income level makes the tasting price a non-issue. The family-friendly component gives it broader appeal across the mix of young families and young professionals. Slightly penalized for distance and the fact that 'festival' events like this recur — unclear if this is a first-year event or established annual.

event_name: Two Door Cinema Club at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb:
Two Door Cinema Club has been making the kind of indie pop that sounds exactly like a specific era of your late 20s, and they're landing at the Coca-Cola Roxy on a Friday night, which is about as good as the timing gets.

If you haven't kept up with them in a while, their newer material has matured into something worth revisiting on its own terms — not just a nostalgia play. The Roxy is one of the better rooms in Atlanta for a show like this, intimate enough to feel close but big enough to actually move around. Friday night, good band, great venue. The math is pretty simple.

Grab tickets and make a full night of it at the Battery.
scoring_notes: Friday night timing is a big plus over the Monday Bleachers show. Two Door Cinema Club's fanbase maps well to the median age 38 Perimeter crowd who came of age with their early catalog. Adult-skewing, no family component needed. The Battery as a destination adds appeal for the mix of young professionals and empty nesters in this audience.

venue: Out of Box Theatre Creator's Den, Marietta
blurb:
Martin McDonagh is the guy who wrote In Bruges. If that tells you something about his taste for dark, uncomfortable, brilliantly written material, then you already know whether The Pillowman is for you.

Out of Box Theatre is staging it now through October 4th in the intimate Creator's Den in Marietta. The play follows a writer whose deeply disturbing short stories catch the attention of a brutal police investigation — and what unfolds from there is the kind of theater that sticks with you for days. McDonagh doesn't let you get comfortable, and a small black-box setting only makes that worse in the best possible way.

This is not a casual night out. It's a genuinely gripping piece of drama performed up close, in a room where there's nowhere to hide from it. If you've been looking for an excuse to actually use a Thursday or Friday night for something worthwhile, this is it. Check Out of Box Theatre's site for showtimes and tickets before the run wraps October 4th.
scoring_notes: The Perimeter audience skews educated and adult, which is exactly who goes to intimate black-box theater productions of McDonagh plays. The limited run (closes October 4) gives it real urgency. Not a family event, but this audience leans adult enough to make that a fit rather than a miss. Marietta is slightly outside core Perimeter coverage but close enough to be relevant.

blurb:
This is not a haunted house. It's weirder and more interesting than that.

The William Root House in Marietta is hosting a Victorian Funeral Midnight Wake on October 9th, a candlelit, guided experience through the historic home where Leonard Simpson actually died on October 11, 1856. You'll move room to room learning about 19th-century embalming and funeral practices, and as midnight hits, the group gathers to recite a poem about death that Simpson himself wrote in 1839. The whole thing is intimate, atmospheric, and genuinely unlike anything else on the calendar this fall.

Space is extremely limited and tickets are $50 per person, purchased in advance only. Guests must be 12 or older, and the program covers adult themes — this is not a trick-or-treat situation. It's the kind of October evening that is actually memorable, not just another fall activity you checked off a list. If this sounds like your speed, move fast.
scoring_notes: Uniqueness score is a 10 — there is nothing else like a candlelit Victorian funeral wake at a historic house where someone actually died. The educated, adult-skewing Perimeter audience is exactly who appreciates this kind of experiential history event. $50 is a complete non-issue for a $105K median household income. Marietta location is a short drive. Limited space creates real urgency.

blurb:
If you have ever watched a dachshund waddle full-speed toward a finish line in a tiny hot dog costume, you already know this is worth your Saturday morning.

Howl-O-Weenie is back at Brook Run Park on September 26th, and it's billed as the largest gathering of dachshunds in the Southeast. That's not marketing fluff — DREAM Dachshund Rescue pulls this off every year and it genuinely draws a crowd. You've got dachshund races, a costume contest (kids' category included), howling competitions, local food trucks, craft vendors, and a silent auction with some genuinely fun prizes, including a raffle for a week-long stay at a dog-friendly beach house in Florida. All ages and all breeds are welcome, so you don't need to own a wiener dog to have a great time. You just need to enjoy watching them.

Brook Run is right in your backyard, admission is free, and this one has the kind of energy that's genuinely hard to manufacture. Get there early, grab a drink from the local brewery on-site, and let the dogs do the rest.
scoring_notes: Brook Run Park is inside the Perimeter coverage area in Dunwoody, making this extremely local. The mix of young families, dog owners, and young professionals all overlaps hard here. Free admission removes friction. The Southeast's largest dachshund gathering is genuinely a unique, annual draw — not a generic park event. Strong fit across the board.
